gen-fs-hoover-fs-asap: Hoover has a funnel-wide throat in its e and a first capital that hardly rises above the letters beside it. Asap follows in sans, easy and readable, with open arcs and a body height close to its capitals.
gen-fs-hoover-fs-epilogue: Hoover's e opens like a funnel, and its first capital barely lifts above the lowercase around it, giving a bookish, confident front. Epilogue's sans body is wire-thin and curvy, friendly and contemporary.
gen-fs-hoover-fs-supreme: Confident is the first word Hoover earns, with its funnel-throated e and a capital that hardly stands taller than its neighbors. And Supreme, a crisp sans, holds its letters open and lays down a heavy-looking band of text.
gen-fs-hoover-general-sans: Bookish and a touch bold, with a funnel-shaped e. Hoover does the swelling bowls, while General Sans runs a smooth plain sans line, its tall x-height filling every line and nothing getting in the way of a curve.
gen-fs-hoover-manrope: Hoover opens with a funnel-wide e and a modest first capital. Its serif voice gives Manrope's sans-serif body a bright, welcoming counterpart, where every curve keeps a clear gap at its mouth and the lowercase n has an arch matching its stem.
gen-fs-hoover-montserrat: Bookish confidence runs through Hoover, from the funnel-wide e to a first capital that barely clears its neighbors. But Montserrat, geometric and friendly, glides along like wire, so paragraphs feel spacious, with generous white space leading into each curve.
gen-fs-hoover-satoshi: Satoshi is a soaring-x-height sans with every stroke cut to one width. And its wide-open e never looks squeezed, so a long page reads smoothly against Hoover's thin joins that stay as sturdy as the stems.
gen-fs-hoover-switzer: Tubular and wire-like with a tall waist line, Switzer is a plain sans with c tips that never creep toward touching. Long stretches read cleanly, with no hairlines and no swells.
gen-fs-kalam-fs-amulya: Amulya reads modern and open, with generous gaps in its sans curves. Kalam, hand-drawn and cozy, is happiest big and short, where its tightly bundled lines can charm.
gen-fs-kalam-fs-neco: Dignified is Neco's whole manner, a serif that swells gently from hairline to stem and never pinches its letters shut. And Kalam is the cozy, hand-drawn voice, best for a handful of lines, like thread set against yarn.
